page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-4 is a compute-skewed virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance executes on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B12 processor providing 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation. Cache hierarchy details include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a 55 MB L3 cache pool. Vector processing support includes standard AVX, but excludes AVX-512 extensions and AMX accelerator sets. Hardware cryptographic features include AES and SHA-NI.

Hardware bundling is minimal, as the e2-highcpu-4 includes no integrated GPUs and provides no local SSD storage. Network configurations do not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external persistent disks and external IP routing to be attached separately. Memory throughput tests show large-block read rates of 46.92 GB/sec and write rates of 33.89 GB/sec, placing it in the average performance tier, though small-block cached transfers and the overall PassMark memory benchmark score fell into weaker tiers.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest processing capacity across both single-threaded and multi-threaded workloads. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 1409.0, representing mid-tier execution efficiency, while the multi-core result of 3168.0 reflects typical entry-level multi-threading for dual-core hyperthreaded layouts. Compression throughput shows 25.69 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip, but multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yields 20.75 GB/sec. Redis performance achieves 2.81 million SET operations per second, and static web serving throughput measures 2.97 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the e2-highcpu-4 provides cost-effective dedicated compute capacity for environments requiring higher CPU thread counts without the expense of large RAM allocations. Its constrained 4.0 GB memory footprint makes it unsuitable for large in-memory databases, dense container clusters, or memory-heavy data pipelines. It is suited for lightweight CPU-bound utility services, microservices, continuous integration build workers, basic batch processing, and proxy or ingress nodes.

The instance includes no local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote persistent storage for disk operations.
